chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine until he becomes intoxicated, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept his prayer from him for forty mornings.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for a Muslim who drinks wine until intoxicated?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific spiritual penalty for consuming khamr to the point of intoxication, stating that Allah will not accept the individual's prayers for forty days. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a temporary suspension of the reward of salah rather than a nullification of the prayer's validity, highlighting the profound impact of major sins on one's connection with the Divine. The chain of transmission (isnad) traces back to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), underscoring the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in defining the consequences of ritual impurity caused by intoxication.
